{{Short description|Concept in universal algebra in mathematics}}

In the area of mathematics known as [[universal algebra]], a '''clone''' is a [[Set (mathematics)|set]] ''C'' of [[finitary]] [[operation (mathematics)|operation]]s on a set ''A'' such that
*''C'' contains all the [[projection (set theory)|projection]]s {{nowrap|{{pi}}<sub>''k''</sub><sup>''n''</sup>: ''A<sup>n</sup>'' → ''A''}}, defined by {{nowrap|1={{pi}}<sub>''k''</sub><sup>''n''</sup>(''x''<sub>1</sub>, …, ''x<sub>n</sub>'') = ''x<sub>k</sub>''}},
*''C'' is closed under [[generalized composition|(finitary multiple) composition]] (or "superposition"):<ref>{{cite journal|title=Menger algebras and clones of terms|author1-first=Klaus|author1-last=Denecke|journal=East–West Journal of Mathematics|year=2003|volume=5|issue=2|issn=1513-489X|page=179|url=http://eastwestmath.org/index.php/ewm/article/view/267}}</ref> if ''f'', ''g''<sub>1</sub>, …, ''g<sub>m</sub>'' are members of ''C'' such that ''f'' is ''m''-ary, and ''g<sub>j</sub>'' is ''n''-ary for all ''j'', then the ''n''-ary operation {{nowrap|1=''h''(''x''<sub>1</sub>, …, ''x<sub>n</sub>'') :=}} {{nowrap|''f''(''g''<sub>1</sub>(''x''<sub>1</sub>, …, ''x<sub>n</sub>''), …, ''g<sub>m</sub>''(''x''<sub>1</sub>, …, ''x<sub>n</sub>''))}} is in ''C''.
The question whether clones should contain nullary operations or not is not treated uniformly in the literature. The classical approach as evidenced by the standard monographs<ref name=FuncRel>{{cite book
|title=Funktionen- und Relationenalgebren. Ein Kapitel der diskreten Mathematik.
|author1-first=Reinhard
|author1-last=Pöschel
|author2-first=Lev A.
|author2-last=Kalužnin
|author2-link=Lev Kaluznin
|language=German
|volume=15
|year=1979
|publisher=VEB Deutscher Verlag der Wissenschaften
|location=Berlin
|series=Mathematische Monographien
}}</ref><ref name=ClonesInUA>{{cite book
|title=Clones in Universal Algebra
|author1-first=Ágnes
|author1-last=Szendrei|author1-link= Ágnes Szendrei
|volume=99
|series=Séminaire de Mathématiques Supérieures
|publisher=Presses de l'Université de Montréal
|location=Montréal, QC
|year=1986
|isbn=978-2-7606-0770-5}}</ref><ref name=Lau>{{cite book
|title=Function Algebras on Finite Sets. A basic course on many-valued logic and clone theory.
|author1-first=Dietlinde
|author1-last=Lau
|publisher=Springer
|location=Berlin
|year=2006
|isbn=978-3-540-36022-3
|series=Springer Monographs in Mathematics
|doi=10.1007/3-540-36023-9}}</ref> on clone theory considers clones only containing at-least-unary operations. However, with only minor modifications (related to the empty invariant relation) most of the usual theory can be lifted to clones allowing nullary operations.<ref name=NullaryClones>{{cite journal
|title=Clones with Nullary Operations
|first=Mike
|last=Behrisch
|editor1-first=John
|editor1-last=Power
|editor2-first=Cai
|editor2-last=Wingfield
|journal=[[Electronic Notes in Theoretical Computer Science]]
|year=2014
|pages=3–35
|volume=303
|issn=1571-0661
|doi=10.1016/j.entcs.2014.02.002|doi-access=free
}}</ref>{{rp|4–5}} The more general concept<ref name=AlgebrasLatticesVarieties>{{cite book
|title=Algebras, Lattices, Varieties
|author1-first=Ralph N.
|author1-last=McKenzie
|author1-link=Ralph McKenzie
|author2-first=George F.
|author2-last=McNulty
|author3-first=Walter F.
|author3-last=Taylor
|publisher=Wadsworth & Brooks/Cole Advanced Books & Software
|location=Monterey, CA
|volume=I
|year=1987
|isbn=978-0-534-07651-1
|page=143}}</ref> includes all clones without nullary operations as subclones of the clone of all at-least-unary operations<ref name=NullaryClones />{{rp|5}} and is in accordance with the custom to allow nullary terms and nullary term operations in universal algebra. Typically, publications studying clones as abstract clones, e.g. in the [[category theoretic]] setting of [[Lawvere]]'s [[Lawvere theory|algebraic theories]], will include nullary operations.<ref name=Trnkova>{{cite journal
|title=All clones are centralizer clones
|author1-first=Věra
|author1-last=Trnková|author1-link= Věra Trnková
|author2-first=Jiří
|author2-last=Sichler
|volume=61
|issue=1
|pages=77–95
|journal=[[Algebra Universalis]]
|year=2009
|issn=0002-5240
|doi=10.1007/s00012-009-0004-4}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|title=On clones determined by their initial segments
|author1-first=Věra
|author1-last=Trnková|author1-link= Věra Trnková
|author2-first=Jiří
|author2-last=Sichler

|journal=[[Cahiers de Topologie et Géométrie Différentielle Catégoriques]]
|year=2008

Given an [[universal algebra|algebra]] in a [[signature (logic)|signature]] ''σ'', the set of operations on its carrier definable by a ''σ''-[[first-order logic#Formation rules|term]] (the ''term functions'') is a clone. Conversely, every clone can be realized as the clone of term functions in a suitable algebra by simply taking the clone itself as source for the signature ''σ'' so that the algebra has the whole clone as its fundamental operations.

If ''A'' and ''B'' are algebras with the same carrier such that every basic function of ''A'' is a term function in ''B'' and vice versa, then ''A'' and ''B'' have the same clone. For this reason, modern universal algebra often treats clones as a representation of algebras that abstracts from their signature.

There is only one clone on the one-element set (there are two if nullary operations are considered). The [[Lattice (order)|lattice]] of clones on a two-element set is countable,<ref name=Rosenberg1974/><ref name=Rosenberg1976/><ref name=ClonesInUA/>{{rp|39}} and has been completely described by [[Emil Post]]<ref name="Post1941">{{cite book
|title=The two-valued iterative systems of mathematical logic
|author1-first=Emil Leon
|author1-last=Post
|author1-link=Emil Leon Post
|publisher=Princeton University Press
|location=Princeton, N. J.
|series=Annals of Mathematics Studies
|volume=5
|year=1941
|mr=0004195
|pages=viii+122}}</ref><ref name=Rosenberg1976/> (see [[Post's lattice]],<ref name=ClonesInUA/>{{rp|37}} which traditionally does not show clones with nullary operations). Clones on larger sets do not admit a simple classification; there are [[cardinality of the continuum|continuum]]-many clones on a finite set of size at least three,<ref name=JanovMuchnik>{{cite journal
|script-title=ru:О существовании ''k''-значных замкнутых классов, не имеющих конечного базиса
|title=O suščestvovanii ''k''-značnyx zamknutyx klassov, ne imejuščix konečnogo bazisa<!--[[Scientific transliteration of Cyrillic]]-->
|trans-title=On the existence of ''k''-valued closed classes having no finite basis
|author1=Юрий Иванович Янов (Jurij Ivanovič Janov)
|author2=Альберт Абрамович Мучник (Aľbert Abramovič Mučnik)
|journal=[[Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR]]
|volume=127|issue=1|year=1959|pages=44–46|mr=0108458|zbl=0100.01001|issn=0002-3264|language=Russian}}</ref><ref name=ClonesInUA/>{{rp|39}} and 2<sup>2<sup>''κ''</sup></sup> (even just maximal,<ref name=Rosenberg1976>{{cite journal
|title=The set of maximal closed classes of operations on an infinite set ''A'' has cardinality 2<sup>2<sup>''&#124;A&#124;''</sup></sup>
|author-first=Ivo G.
|author-last=Rosenberg
|journal=[[Archiv der Mathematik]]|volume=27|year=1976|issue=6|page=562|publisher=Springer (Birkhäuser)|location=Basel|issn=0003-889X|mr=0429700|zbl=0345.02010|doi=10.1007/BF01224718}}</ref><ref name=ClonesInUA/>{{rp|39}} i.e. precomplete) clones on an infinite set of [[cardinality]]&nbsp;''κ''.<ref name=Rosenberg1974>{{cite journal
|title=Some maximal closed classes of operations on infinite sets
|author-first=Ivo G.

== Abstract clones ==
[[Philip Hall]] introduced the concept of ''abstract clone''.<ref>{{cite book|author1-first=Paul Moritz|author1-last=Cohn|author1-link=Paul Cohn|title=Universal Algebra|edition=2nd|year=1981|publisher=D. Reidel Publishing Co.|location=Dordrecht-Boston, Mass.|volume=6|series=Mathematics and its Applications|isbn=978-90-277-1254-7|page=127}}</ref> An abstract clone is different from a concrete clone in that the set ''A'' is not given.
Formally, an abstract clone comprises 
*a set ''C<sub>n</sub>'' for each natural number ''n'',
*elements {{pi}}<sub>''k'',''n''</sub> in ''C<sub>n</sub>'' for all ''k''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''n'', and 
*a family of functions ∗:''C''<sub>''m''</sub> × (''C''<sub>''n''</sub>)<sup>''m''</sup> → ''C''<sub>''n''</sub> for all ''m'' and ''n''
such that 
* ''c'' * ({{pi}}<sub>1,''n''</sub>, …, {{pi}}<sub>''n'',''n''</sub>) = ''c''  
* {{pi}}<sub>''k'',''m''</sub> * (''c''<sub>1</sub>, …, ''c''<sub>''m''</sub>) = ''c''<sub>''k''</sub>  
* ''c'' * (''d''<sub>1</sub> * (''e''<sub>1</sub>, …, ''e''<sub>''n''</sub>), …, ''d''<sub>''m''</sub> * (''e''<sub>1</sub>, …, ''e''<sub>''n''</sub>)) = (''c'' * (''d''<sub>1</sub>, …, ''d''<sub>''m''</sub>)) * (''e''<sub>1</sub>, …, ''e''<sub>''n''</sub>).

Any concrete clone determines an abstract clone in the obvious manner.

Any [[algebraic theory]] determines an abstract clone where ''C<sub>n</sub>'' is the set of terms (up to equivalence) in ''n'' variables, {{pi}}<sub>''k'',''n''</sub> are variables, and ∗ is [[Substitution (logic)|substitution]]. Two theories determine isomorphic clones if and only if the corresponding categories of algebras are [[isomorphism of categories|isomorphic]]. Conversely every abstract clone determines an algebraic theory with an ''n''-ary operation for each element of ''C<sub>n</sub>''. This gives a bijective correspondence between abstract clones and algebraic theories.

Every abstract clone ''C'' induces a [[Lawvere theory]] in which the morphisms ''m''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''n'' are the elements of (''C<sub>m</sub>'')<sup>''n''</sup>. This induces a bijective correspondence between Lawvere theories and abstract clones.
